common_name: Towering Inferno Cardinal Flower (Giant Self-Seeded Cardinal Flower)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring into consistently moist to boggy, humus-rich soil near a pond edge, stream bank, or rain garden; stake or site out of strong wind until the thick basal stem establishes, since the extreme height needs a sturdy root system to stay upright.

directions: Towering Inferno is a 2022 Plant Delights Nursery/Juniper Level Botanic Garden introduction, discovered as an exceptionally tall, thick-stemmed plant growing within a large patch of self-sown cardinal flower at the garden in North Carolina. Established clumps can reach a remarkable 7 feet in flower, well above the species norm, topped from late summer into fall with the same bright scarlet, hummingbird-pollinated spikes typical of cardinal flower. Give it consistently moist to wet, rich soil in sun to light shade; plants grown in drier or leaner conditions will not approach the cultivar's signature height. Because seedlings from self-sown seed usually revert toward typical species height, propagate by division to keep the giant stature true.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden catalog

common_name: Sorak Ligularia (Mt. Sorak Korean Leopard Plant)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring into consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part sun to shade; established clumps tolerate summer heat better than many ligularias and can be divided every few years to spread the bold-leaved clump.

directions: Sorak traces to Dan Hinkley's 1997 Korean plant-collecting expedition to Mt. Sorak in Korea, and was later introduced into the nursery trade through Plant Delights Nursery/Juniper Level Botanic Garden. Bold, heart-shaped green leaves resprout vigorously each spring, building a substantial, textural clump that stays handsome through summer heat better than many Ligularia selections. In late summer, slender spikes of yellow daisy flowers rise to roughly 2.5 feet above the foliage, drawing butterflies to the shade border. Keep soil evenly moist to boggy and out of hot afternoon sun to prevent wilting of the large leaves.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden catalog
